problem_statement: Saltmarsh Almanac is a coastal-naturalist field journal built on the Fuwari Astro theme (Astro 5 with a Svelte island, Tailwind CSS and Swup page transitions): a homepage that lists the journal's entries as post cards beside an author profile sidebar, an /archive page that groups every entry by year, individual entry pages under /posts/<slug>, and an /about page, all wrapped in a shared Navbar (Home / Archive / About / Field log), a profile SideBar and a Footer. The journal hosts its own reading tool: a 'Reading room' category filter that sits directly above the post-card list. It is a labelled row of category chips (All entries plus the journal's standing strands — Field Notes, Almanac, Tidewatch, Species, Craft) each showing its entry count, and a live readout that reports how many of the nine entries are showing for the chosen strand, in the form 'Showing N of 9 entries . <Category>'. The filter is promoted on every surface that frames the reading room: the home post-list, the archive and the about intro. Ship the Reading-room filter so it (1) appears above the reading surface on the home page AND the archive AND the about page, (2) lays out its chip row responsively so no reading surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone, (3) matches the Saltmarsh Almanac card styling (legible pill chips keyed to the theme tokens, a clearly highlighted active chip) rather than a dark near-black slab or an overlapping pile of chips, and (4) keeps the readout in sync so a reader who clicks the Field Notes chip sees the list narrow to the three Field Notes entries and the readout update to 'Showing 3 of 9 entries . Field Notes' — it must re-read the live matched set, not show a stale captured value. Keep the rest of the theme — the navigation, the profile sidebar, existing entry content, the year-grouped archive, RSS and the Astro build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Reading room' category filter above the reading surface so it renders on the home post-list AND the archive AND the about page (a shared component, not a per-page copy).

The filter shows a 'Reading room' label, a chip row of All entries plus the journal's standing categories (Field Notes, Almanac, Tidewatch, Species, Craft) each with its entry count, and a live 'Showing N of 9 entries . <Category>' readout.
The chip row must wrap responsively so no reading surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).

Style the filter in the Saltmarsh Almanac card language (legible pill chips keyed to the theme tokens, a clearly highlighted active chip), not a dark near-black slab and not a collapsed pile of overlapping chips.

Wire the chip clicks so that clicking a category (for example Field Notes) re-filters the home post-list to the matching entries AND re-syncs the readout to 'Showing N of 9 entries . <Category>' (for example 'Showing 3 of 9 entries . Field Notes'); marking the chip active is not sufficient — the readout must re-read the live matched set, not a stale captured value.

Preserve the navigation (Home / Archive / About / Field log), the profile sidebar, the footer, the year-grouped archive, the existing entry/about content, images and the Astro build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Implement the Reading-room filter as a shared component so a single source of truth reaches the home post-list, the archive and the about page; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The chip row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.

The filter must adopt the Fuwari theme tokens (the --primary accent, --card-bg panel, the theme's rounded card radius, text color ramp and font family) so it reads as part of the journal; the active chip must be legible (high-contrast primary fill), and the chip row must stay a tidy wrapping row, not a negative-margin overlapping pile.
Keep the readout in sync with the CURRENT filter selection after every click by recomputing the visible count from the matched set, so it can never go stale relative to the shown entries.
Do not remove or regress the navigation, the profile sidebar, existing entry/about content, the year-grouped archive, RSS or the Astro build.
state_constraints: desktop_home, mobile_home and tablet_home protect the homepage post-list and profile sidebar across viewports, and carry the Reading-room filter on the home page (D2 cross-page presence, D3 filter layout, D6 mobile overflow).

desktop_archive and desktop_about carry the Reading-room filter on the archive and about pages (D2 cross-page presence); the reference promotes it on both, the negative controls omit it on one or both.
desktop_post protects the existing entry reading surface (title, sections and body copy) unchanged.

home_filter_fieldnotes clicks the Field Notes category chip on the home post-list; the list must narrow to the three Field Notes entries and the readout must re-sync to 'Showing 3 of 9 entries . Field Notes' (the interaction terminal state).
The mobile home state (mobile_home) is the horizontal-overflow discriminator: the reference reports 0 overflow while the fixed-width negative controls overflow.

change_completion: The Reading-room filter is present above the reading surface on the home post-list AND the archive AND the about page (the shared component reaches all three routes).

After clicking the Field Notes category chip on the home post-list, the list narrows to the three Field Notes entries and the readout re-syncs to 'Showing 3 of 9 entries . Field Notes' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Showing 9 of 9 entries . All entries'.
design_consistency: The filter on the home states matches the reference's card/pill editorial styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), with a legible active chip and a tidy wrapping chip row, not a dark near-black slab or an overlapping pile.
The filter adopts the Fuwari theme tokens (--primary, --card-bg, the card radius and font family) so it reads as part of the journal across every surface.
responsive: No captured reading surface overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the chip row wraps.
desktop_home and tablet_home keep the filter and post-list readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: The navigation (Home / Archive / About / Field log), the profile sidebar, the footer and the year-grouped archive remain present and functional.
The existing entry/about content, images, RSS and the Astro build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

metadata.design_goal: add the journal's own on-brand 'Reading room' category filter across the post-listing surfaces with a live count readout, while keeping the navigation, profile sidebar, year-grouped archive and Astro build stable
metadata.source_repo_kind: Fuwari Astro 5 editorial blog theme with a Svelte island, shared Navbar/SideBar/Footer, a homepage post-card list, a year-grouped archive, entry routes and an about page, using Tailwind CSS theme tokens and local images
metadata.selected_repo_reason: saicaca/fuwari is a runnable Astro 5 + Svelte + Tailwind editorial blog; it builds to static output offline and hosts a natural state-continuity modification on the blog's OWN post-listing category filter spanning a mobile-overflow defect, cross-page presence, filter-panel layout, and chip-click count wiring.

author_notes: slot_144 rebuilt to a genre-native L4 on the saicaca Fuwari Astro editorial-blog theme (rebranded as the Saltmarsh Almanac coastal-naturalist journal). The lever is the journal's OWN post-card list and its native 'Reading room' category filter (All entries plus five standing categories over the nine real journal entries, with a live 'Showing N of 9 entries . <Category>' readout), not a bolted-on metric rail. Each entry carries a real category (Field Notes, Almanac, Tidewatch, Species, Craft) in its Astro content frontmatter. The filter is a Svelte island hardened to fail four orthogonal acceptance gates in the bad solution. Lever 1 (D6 no_horizontal_overflow): the chip row uses a fixed-width non-wrapping track that overflows a 390px phone; the reference wraps it. Lever 2 (D2 dom_assertions, cross-page): the 'Reading room' filter must be promoted on the home post-list, the archive and the about page; reference promotes it on all three, baseline only on home, bad on home and archive (about forgotten), so both negative controls fail the presence assertion on the omitted pages. Lever 3 (D3 visual_regression): the bad filter panel collapses — the chips are pulled together with large negative margins so they shingle and stagger into an overlapping pile, the panel and chip labels are near-black on near-black (illegible), and the heading and readout are buried — failing pixelmatch/ssim/block fidelity against the tidy reference panel. Lever 4 (D4 interaction_assertions): the bad chip click flips .is-active and re-filters the cards but reads the readout from a value captured once at mount, so after the Field Notes click the readout stays 'Showing 9 of 9 entries . All entries'. Three leg-varying files (src/components/ReadingRoomFilter.svelte, src/styles/reading-room.css, src/constants/readingRoomSurfaces.ts) live in suggested_files; the entry content, images and category taxonomy are shared byte-identically across legs. Built offline as static Astro output (astro build plus pagefind) served by a static file server, with the fonts and entry images local and no network calls; that infrastructure is identical across legs. The photoshoot and design keep an image/svg avatar and cover artwork on the card surfaces.
